workflow.title: Review project folders before cleaning developer storage with SpaceBroom
workflow.primaryIntent: A developer on macOS 14+ wants to distinguish large project directories from explicitly reviewed cleanup categories, without treating every large folder as disposable.
workflow.descriptionDirection: Use Space Lens for orientation, inspect a candidate's purpose and rebuild/backup cost, then review an explicit action. Duplicate exclusions and Trash exceptions matter more than an advertised total.
outline: Conclusion: file size is a reason to investigate, not permission to remove
Top visual: rights-cleared Space Lens asset with vendor credit, no invented measured results
Follow the documented folder-size navigation; do not call this a hands-on walkthrough
Separate project originals, rebuildable caches and vendor duplicate exclusions
Check confirmation, permanent-action warning and conditional history restore
When a one-time cleanup tool fits, and when recurring-growth/process investigation may justify Breathing Room, which we build
Second visual: current-source Breathing Room Space preview with example-data caption; bounded preview/runtime/hosted caveats
workflow.interactionPass: Plan a non-executing decision checklist: Is this original work? Is a current backup available? What is the rebuild/download cost? Is the action Trash or permanent? Is the location permission-limited? No filesystem access, uploads or delete buttons.
workflow.differentiation: Project-preservation and restore-precondition workflow, not a renamed generic junk-cleaner comparison or the price matrix expanded into filler.

advantagesAndTradeoffs.wording: Documented duplicate/uninstaller and direct folder-navigation workflows, plus a one-time version-1 licence, may fit a bounded manual cleanup task.

macOS 14 minimum; cleanup paid after trial; annual minimum/notice terms and permanent-operation exceptions require attention. Process grouping and recurring-growth capabilities remain unverified, not absent.
The source-implemented grouped process and activity views may better match a question about which app is active while storage changes, provided sampled/inferred attribution limits are understood.

Preview release is not notarized, Python is required for inventory, physical Intel/clean-machine behavior is unverified, and authenticated hosted AI is neither entirely offline nor unlimited by evidence. Daily care requires the app to remain running.
